claim: Across meta-analyses, formal strategic planning has a small-to-moderate positive link with firm performance (Boyd 1991 k=29; George 2019 31 studies/87 correlations, 'positive, moderate'; Hamann 2022 k=183). Exact pooled r values were not read. Gap search: Boyd 1991 pools 29 samples / 2,496 firms and reports 'modest' correlations; George 2019 (31 studies, 87 correlations) is a public-administration journal paper. Pooled r, CI, I2 still unread (publisher full text blocked).
agent_test: Field result, no direct test. Use as a prior that structured option work is not harmful.

claim: The planning-performance effect is fragile to publication bias: Shea-Van Fossen 2006 (39 studies, 5,223 firms) drops from d=0.257 to 0.109 (CI -0.235 to 0.242) after trim-and-fill. One source, abstract level. Gap search could not read any second source for bias correction (Hamann and George full texts blocked).

claim: The effect depends on context: stronger for effectiveness measures and formal planning (George 2019); stronger in manufacturing, larger firms, high uncertainty-avoidance countries and high environmental uncertainty (Hamann 2022). This goes against the folk claim that planning fails in turbulence.
agent_test: Scale planning budget with task uncertainty; compare fixed vs adaptive allocation at equal tokens.

claim: Small-firm and new-venture evidence is mostly observational (Delmar and Shane 223 ventures; Brinckmann 2010 meta-analysis of contextual factors). No effect sizes were read. Gap search: Delmar and Shane abstract (223 Swedish ventures, planning lowers disbanding) and Brinckmann title/scope only; no effect sizes obtained.
agent_test: n/a

claim: Teaching entrepreneurs a scientific hypothesis-testing approach (Camuffo 2020 RCT, 116 startups, 59 treated / 57 control, 10 sessions, about one year) improved performance and pivoting vs an intuition control. A large replication (SMJ 2024, four RCTs, 759 firms) confirms more idea termination and a non-linear effect on pivots (few pivots beat none or many); its abstract does not restate a revenue gain. A second Italian trial (250 to 257 startups) is registered with no results in the registry, and an independent Uruguay replication (2 x 116) is running to Sept 2026. Same research group; tests hypothesis testing, not planning.
agent_test: Compare plan-then-act vs hypothesis-and-test steps on forecasting tasks at equal tokens.

claim: People underestimate completion time (planning fallacy): 37 students predicted 33.9 days vs actual 55.5, about 30% finished within prediction. Read via Wikipedia only.
agent_test: Ask the agent for inside-view vs reference-class estimates of task duration; measure calibration.

claim: Sampling many candidates and selecting with an external checker gives large gains: ToT Game of 24 74% (b=5) vs CoT 4.0% and CoT-SC 9.0%; Large Language Monkeys SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples (both verified in full text). Needs a checkable answer.
agent_test: Fixed token budget: one long chain vs N short samples plus verifier on a checkable task.

claim: Model-scored selection is the weak link: LLMs do not self-correct intrinsically (GPT-3.5 keeps its answer 74.7%, more correct-to-wrong changes) and self-consistency lowered scores on Blocksworld planning prompts.
agent_test: Compare model-judged vs external-verifier selection at equal N.

claim: Plan-then-solve prompting gives small gains: PS+ average 76.7 vs zero-shot CoT 70.4 on six math sets, PS alone 72.9 (b29 wrongly said 73.5, which is PoT); StrategyQA only 63.8 to 65.4. Old model, math only.
agent_test: Plan-first vs direct prompt at equal tokens on a current model.

claim: Plain LLMs plan poorly on classical planning: PlanBench GPT-4 34.3% valid plans (206/600), Instruct-GPT3 6.8%; o1-preview 52.8% on Mystery Blocksworld, 37.3% randomized; Fast Downward 100%.
agent_test: Route planning subtasks to a symbolic solver; compare with LLM-only.

claim: An external verifier loop lifts LLM planning (LLM-Modulo: Blocks World 82% in 15 rounds, Logistics 70%) but fails where the model cannot propose plausible candidates (Mystery about 10%).
agent_test: Back-prompt with verifier output vs plain resampling at equal tokens.

claim: Explicit plans help code generation: self-planning HumanEval Pass@1 60.3 vs CoT 53.9; ground-truth plan 74.4, so plan quality is the bottleneck.
agent_test: Score plan quality separately from execution quality.

claim: A planner plus replanning raises agent success on web tasks (Plan-and-Act WebArena-Lite 9.85 to 29.63 to 57.58%) but uses a trained planner; TheAgentCompany best agent reaches only 30.3% full completion.
agent_test: Replan-on-failure vs fixed plan, no training, equal tokens.

claim: LLM business-simulation results are high variance: Vending-Bench Claude 3.5 Sonnet mean $2,217.93 (min $476) vs human $844.05 (one run), GPT-4o $335.46 (verified). Long-horizon coherence, not plan quality, drives failures.
agent_test: Run 5+ seeds and report the minimum as well as the mean.

claim: Reasoning models show a complexity pattern: plain models win at low complexity, reasoning models at medium, both collapse at high (Illusion of Thinking). Critics on token limits were not opened.
agent_test: Vary difficulty; compare extra reasoning vs none.

claim: LLMs generate and evaluate strategic options, with caveats. Girotra 2023 (read in full): 400 ideas, purchase intent students 40.4% vs GPT-4 46.8% vs GPT-4 with examples 49.3%; 35 of the top 40 ideas from GPT-4; about 800 ideas/hour at about $0.63 per idea (human alone about $25). Meincke 2024: plain GPT-4 pools are less diverse than human group pools (cosine similarity 0.255 to 0.432 vs 0.243); CoT closes most of the gap. Doshi 2024 (abstract only): single LLM evaluations of 60 business models are inconsistent; aggregated ones resemble expert rankings. Correlations with expert rankings still not obtained.
agent_test: Option count and quality at equal tokens against expert rankings.

claim: Comprehensiveness (many options before selecting) is the core mechanism claimed by the field, but the founding studies (Fredrickson and Mitchell 1984, Dean and Sharfman 1996, Nutt 1993 N=163) were not read. The claimed boundary (instability) is unverified. Gap search: retrieval failed again (JSTOR); still unread.

claim: Multi-agent business-simulation gains (BusiAgent +122% analysis, 100 experts) rest on expert ratings of the authors' own system and BLEU. Weak evidence.

claim: Only a minority of large firms use their formal plan for their most important decisions. McKinsey Quarterly 2006 survey (N=796 executives, firms with revenue of at least $500M): over 75% have a formal planning process, fewer than 25% say it is key to their most important decisions; 52% say a small senior group including the CEO decides, 23% say they decide with the formal process; fewer than half are satisfied with their strategy approach.
schema_part: G (the option step must bind the final choice)
agent_test: Check that the final answer cites which generated options it chose between and why.

claim: Distinct plans before acting raise best-of-k success when a checker exists. PlanSearch (LiveCodeBench pass@200: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 55.6 to 77.0, GPT-4o 60.6 to 73.0; with public-test filtering PlanSearch reaches 77.1% at pass@20 vs 77.0% at pass@200 without filtering) and idea diversity predicts the gain. Pass@1 can fall. Compute-normalised plots agree with the equal-attempt plots (authors' statement). No study found that links option count to final decision quality on open-ended strategy tasks (gap 3 stays open).
agent_test: Count distinct ideas (LLM-judged similarity) in the option list and check against the checker or a panel's score at equal tokens.

claim: Extra reasoning is not always better for current models. Chain-of-thought lowers accuracy in tasks like implicit statistical learning (o1-preview 57.7% vs GPT-4o 94.0%, -36.3 points on a 440-problem subset; GPT-4o -23.1); longer reasoning in frontier models can lower accuracy on distractor, spurious-feature and constraint tasks (Gema 2025). In a many-feature choice task reasoning mostly helped. No equal-token plan-first versus direct test on open-ended judgment found.
schema_part: G (budget cap, test the plan step)
agent_test: Run plan-first versus direct at equal tokens on open-ended judgment items; record the paired difference.

claim: A difficulty-scaled thinking budget has measured support for LLMs on math: Snell 2024 uses about 4x less compute than best-of-N by choosing the method per difficulty bin; search hurts on easy items and gives little on the hardest. This echoes Hamann 2022 (planning pays more at high uncertainty) but nobody tested it for firms-like decisions.
agent_test: Give a small budget to easy items and a large one to medium items; compare with a flat budget at equal total tokens.

claim: Without a ground-truth checker, the best-measured substitutes are aggregation and judges. A crowd of 12 LLMs matches a 925-person human crowd (Brier 0.20 vs 0.19, 31 questions); GPT-4 as judge agrees with humans over 80% of the time but has position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias; single LLM evaluations of business models are inconsistent and only aggregates resemble experts (Doshi, abstract).
agent_test: Compare one-call selection with the mean of 5 or more calls (varied order, role) against an expert key.
